label: Customers
name: customers
description: A registry of customers: the routes talk to a REST API (mockapi.io); customers are imported from and exported to CSV files through the blob registry. Reads are public; writes are for signed-in employees holding the registrar role, identified by our own token, issued by the included access tree (@wilanis/access) at /api/v1/auth-employees against a directory this project binds (account holders sign in at /api/v1/auth-customers and hold a token too, but no write). Preferences live in the session. A command-line greeting is gated by a one-time code. Plugins come from npm packages named by "from".

otp.description: a one-time code: printed by the issue-otp command in this example, delivered out of band in a real tree -- the binding of access.port.json#deliverCode decides

includes.description: sign-in, sessions, policies and the one-time code, as a tree of their own; identity.port.json is bound below, in features/directories

startup.label: Prepare the customer store
startup.description: Make storage ready once, before anything reads it: under local that creates the collections the store declares, and under live there is nothing to create, so it reads the collection once. Only a startup step prepares, and only because project.json says so.

startup.label: Reach the customer store
startup.description: Read the customers once before the HTTP server opens, so a tree whose storage is unreachable refuses to serve instead of answering every route with a fault. The port is bound per profile, so this checks whatever storage the profile chose.

startup.label: Reach the guard's memory
startup.description: Read one session through @auth/state.port.json before the HTTP server opens, so a tree whose sessions and challenges cannot be reached refuses to serve rather than refusing every signed-in caller. No session is kept under this key, so a reachable store answers nothing; the profile's binding decides which store that is.

startup.label: Watch for changes
startup.description: Serve the tree again whenever a document changes, without closing the port. A change that does not pass wilanis check is reported and the last good tree keeps answering.

startup.label: Keep the schedule
startup.description: Fire the scheduled triggers of this tree, each at the instants its cron expression names. Delete this step and nothing is scheduled: the nightly digest is a document either way, and it fires because project.json asks for a scheduler, never because the trigger exists. One process runs it here; several instances would give it a lease.

startup.label: Export traces
startup.description: Send every run this tree serves to an OpenTelemetry collector at localhost:4318, as spans. Delete this step and nothing is exported: traces leave the process because project.json says so, never because the runtime decided a tree should phone home. It is not required, because no collector is running when you clone this example: the step only subscribes, so it succeeds with nothing listening, and every batch it then cannot send is said once in the log and dropped rather than delaying or failing the run whose trace it was. Run `wilanis run <trigger> example --trace` to read the same spans on your terminal with no collector at all.

startup.label: Listen
startup.description: Open the HTTP port and answer this tree's routes. Delete this step and nothing listens: a tree serves because it says so, never because a trigger exists.

live.description: The real customer API, and the directories written in the connections. A production profile binds identity.port.json to a binding whose connections are an OIDC issuer and LDAP; nothing else changes.

local.description: Everything in this process: the customers kept in memory, and the directories written in the connections. Nothing reaches the network, so `wilanis start example --profile local` serves the same routes with no upstream at all.

production.description: The customers in PostgreSQL, and the directories written in the connections. The same routes, policies, shapes and business graphs as every other profile: what changes is which binding meets customer.port.json, and through it which connection the records live behind. The startup step prepares the database before the port opens, so a tree whose database is unreachable refuses to serve rather than answering every route with a fault.
